head: Samsung Phone app may warn about spoofed calls from your contacts
dek: Code in Samsung's Phone app points to a Caller device check that would warn you when a call showing a saved contact's name may not come from that person's phone, Android Authority found. Samsung hasn't announced it, and it may not ship.
details: The check would send a hidden RCS message of up to 48 bytes to the contact's device to confirm the call is real; if it can't, you'd get a notice that the call may be harmful. Contact details and call content aren't sent to a server, according to the code, but both phones need an active RCS connection. It only covers saved contacts, not unknown numbers. Google added a similar check to Pixel phones in June 2026 and said it would bring it to other devices.
where: Samsung Galaxy phones, possibly with One UI 9.5; found in work-in-progress code, not confirmed
means: Scammers sometimes fake a family member's number. If this ships, your Galaxy could flag those calls before you trust them.
todo: Nothing to change yet. Until then, if a call from a family member asks for money or codes, hang up and call them back on their usual number.
thumb_words: SAMSUNG TO FLAG FAKE CONTACT CALLS?
